evidence.section: 3.1. Microstructure analysis of alloys with different states

parameters.atmosphere: air resistance furnace, argon gas flame-retarded

evidence.section: 2. Experimental
evidence.quote: the solid solution temperature is selected at 500°C for 12 h for Mg-Gd-Y alloy. The solution treatment process is conducted in an air resistance furnace and flame-retarded by argon gas, and all samples directly move from furnace into cold water which quenches them, followed by rolling.

evidence.section: 2. Experimental
evidence.quote: The amount of deformation of the alloy during rolling is 5%. After 8 passes rolling, the thickness of the alloy is 1.6 mm, that is, the cumulative deformation is 40%.

evidence.section: 3.2. Effect of annealing process on microstructure of GWQ1032K magnesium alloy
evidence.quote: the rolled alloy was annealed at 300°C, 350 °C, 400 °C and 450 °C for 1800s, and then the microstructure was observed.

evidence.section: 3.2. Effect of annealing process on microstructure of GWQ1032K magnesium alloy
evidence.quote: the optimum annealing treatment process of the GWQ1032K magnesium alloy is annealed at 530°C for 20 s.

evidence.section: 3.1. Microstructure analysis of alloys with different states
evidence.quote: the microstructure of as-cast alloy is mainly composed of gray-white magnesium matrix(α-Mg) and black eutectic phase(α+β)

evidence.section: 3.1. Microstructure analysis of alloys with different states
evidence.quote: the morphology of eutectic phase is irregular, mostly about 2μm. The structure and lattice parameters of eutectic phase corresponding to Mg5Gd phase are calculated

evidence.section: 3.1. Microstructure analysis of alloys with different states
evidence.quote: after 40% cold rolling deformation, a large number of twins appear in the grain of the alloy

evidence.section: 3.2. Effect of annealing process on microstructure of GWQ1032K magnesium alloy
evidence.quote: When the heating temperature rises to 450°C (as shown in figure 2(d)), the number of new recrystallized grains produced at the twin boundary is significantly increased. It can be seen that all twins have recrystallized and no twins remained. The recrystallized grains are equiaxed.

evidence.section: 3.2. Effect of annealing process on microstructure of GWQ1032K magnesium alloy
evidence.quote: After annealing for 20 s, the grain is the finest and uniform, about 30 ∼ 70 μm. At this point, the grain appears equiaxed.

evidence.section: 3.2. Effect of annealing process on microstructure of GWQ1032K magnesium alloy
evidence.quote: there are a large number of second phases with high rare earth content in the grain boundary and the interior of the grains. The precipitated phase along the grain boundary distribution has a large size and tends to be connected together. Meanwhile, the precipitates in the interior are mainly in the form of irregular particles and vary in size.

evidence.section: 3.2. Effect of annealing process on microstructure of GWQ1032K magnesium alloy
evidence.quote: chemical composition of precipitation were basically determined according to the atomic structure is Mg2RE (or Ag).

evidence.section: 3.2. Effect of annealing process on microstructure of GWQ1032K magnesium alloy
evidence.quote: high-density dislocations are introduced into the alloy after cold-rolling deformation

evidence.section: 3.2. Effect of annealing process on microstructure of GWQ1032K magnesium alloy
evidence.quote: Most of the parallel twin boundaries do not show changes.

evidence.section: 3.2. Effect of annealing process on microstructure of GWQ1032K magnesium alloy
evidence.quote: the hardness of the alloy is reduced by 25.1%, from 115.9 HV in the as-rolled state to 86.8 HV.

evidence.section: 3.2. Effect of annealing process on microstructure of GWQ1032K magnesium alloy
evidence.quote: When the alloy is annealed at 450 °C for 1800 s, the hardness of the alloy is reduced by 25.1%, from 115.9 HV in the as-rolled state to 86.8 HV.

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: it further proved that the effect of fine crystal reinforcing and precipitation reinforcing of cold rolled magnesium alloys could be maximized by high temperature rapid annealing treatment.

evidence.section: 3.2. Effect of annealing process on microstructure of GWQ1032K magnesium alloy
evidence.quote: According to the Hall-Petch relationship[19], the fine grains can significantly increases the strength of the alloy, and can shorten the dislocation slip stroke, relieve stress concentration near the grain boundary, and improve plasticity.
